title: Oil eases to $97 while Yemen jumps to 70 and Hormuz stays Red

topMovers.label: Brent eases vs last week
topMovers.cause: World Monitor Sep 21 pulse: Brent $97.43 (−1.87% day; down from Sep 19’s $99.29). WTI $94.00 (−2.16%). IR/SA feeds: oil at a 1-week low on Iran-war diplomacy hopes and ‘surprisingly strong’ crude flows — Hormuz score still 70 Red.

topMovers.label: Yemen instability +10
topMovers.cause: YE High 70 Rising +9 (was Elevated 60 on Sep 19). Houthi ballistic-missile attempt on Riyadh confirmed in SA/YE feeds; Bab el-Mandeb stays 40 Yellow.

topMovers.label: Iran Rising +4 to High 70
topMovers.cause: IR 67 → 70 High Rising +4. Iran rules out reopening Hormuz / US talks until conditions met; US leaves war open-ended while Qatar pushes talks. Hormuz disruption still 70 Red.

topMovers.label: Ukraine eases Critical
topMovers.cause: UA Critical 82 (was 86 Rising +2 last week). Still top of the board. Duma election week: ‘largest ever’ drone strike on Moscow; Ukraine Pelican ballistic first use; Sep HAPI Ukraine-war pulse still 5,453 events / 2,222 fatalities.

topMovers.label: Hormuz + Kerch still Red
topMovers.cause: Both unchanged at 70 Red on the Sep 21 chokepoint board. Hormuz transit WoW +68.2% (counts recovering, score stuck); Kerch −100% WoW, Azov grain still constrained. 7 of 13 chokepoints Yellow or Red.

energy.summary: Grounded in World Monitor crawlable-live-pulse-2026-09-21.json (capturedAt 2026-09-21; quotesAsOf 04:51 UTC; live MCP/API still needs Balu’s X-WorldMonitor-Key). Brent $97.43 (−1.87%), WTI $94.00 (−2.16%), US hub nat gas $2.889 (−0.79%). Vs Sep 19 baseline: Brent −$1.86, WTI −$2.08. Soft tape on diplomacy hopes and strong flows, not a Hormuz unwind — score still 70 Red; Iran says Hormuz stays closed until conditions met.
cascadingImpacts: Hormuz Red + Iran diplomacy tape → crude softens but war premium stays → inflation path still energy-linked
bullets: Brent $97.43 and WTI $94.00 on the Sep 21 WM quote panel (vs $99.29 / $96.08 on Sep 19).
Hormuz disruption 70/100 (Red); week-over-week transit movement +68.2% where published.
IR/SA feeds: oil at a 1-week low on Iran-war diplomacy hopes; CNBC notes crude flows ‘surprisingly strong’.

ai.summary: AI items on the geopolitics board are capital and safety talks, not a frontier-model drop. GB feed: UK Sovereign AI Fund still in talks on a £500m drug-discovery raise; Amazon taps the UK bond market for the first time to fund AI buildout. CN feed: Bessent proposes US–China AI safety notifications ahead of a Trump–Xi summit. Power cost from the war-energy premium remains the cascade into infra pace.
cascadingImpacts: Energy tax → power cost → AI infra pace; US–China AI safety talk → compliance drag on model rollout
bullets: UK Sovereign AI Fund / £500m drug-discovery item and Amazon UK-bond AI funding in the GB feed.
Bessent US–China AI safety notifications proposal in the CN developments feed; no verified frontier-model launch on this pulse.

war.summary: Three sleeves moved: Yemen jumped to High 70 Rising +9 on the Riyadh missile attempt; Iran climbed to High 70 Rising +4 while ruling out a Hormuz reopen; Ukraine eased to Critical 82 but stayed #1 with election-week drone pressure on Moscow and first Pelican use. RU High 76 (stable). Hormuz and Kerch remain 70 Red; Bab el-Mandeb 40 Yellow; Suez 35 Yellow. Sep HAPI month pulses unchanged in totals: Ukraine-war 5,453 / 2,222; Hormuz–Gulf 527 / 251; Red Sea 659 / 960.
cascadingImpacts: Iran/Hormuz + Yemen/Houthi + Ukraine → Red chokepoints → insurance, ships, oil premium
bullets: Hormuz and Kerch both 70 Red; Suez 35 Yellow; Bab el-Mandeb 40 Yellow; 7 of 13 Yellow or Red.
Ukraine Critical 82; Iran High 70 Rising +4; Yemen High 70 Rising +9; Russia High 76.
Pulse headlines: Russian State Duma election with ruling-party majority track; largest-ever drone attack on Moscow; Houthi strike attempt on Riyadh.

food.summary: No FAO index print in the public quote panel. Transmission still freight + war-risk: Kerch −100% WoW with Azov grain constrained; Red Sea / Bab el-Mandeb Yellow keeps insurance elevated. YE dengue outbreak near Dhubab al-Mandeb is a local health item, not a global grain print.
cascadingImpacts: Kerch/Red Sea risk → grain and food freight with a lag
bullets: Kerch Strait −100% week-over-week movement on the published pulse; Azov grain route constrained.
No FAO-grade print in the Sep 21 quote panel.

transport.summary: Maritime corridor risk still sets the transport map. Hormuz Red with transit rebound (+68.2% WoW), Kerch Red and near-zero movement, Suez Yellow, Cape congestion High as the alternate (+15.3% WoW). JP typhoon (Dujuan) is a weather ops item for eastern Japan, not a chokepoint score change. China shipbuilding orders nearly triple on Iran-war windfall (Nikkei) — capacity response to the same war map.
cascadingImpacts: Chokepoints + Gulf/Red Sea war → ships and aviation → delayed boxes
bullets: 7 of 13 chokepoints Yellow or Red on the Sep 21 public snapshot (2 Red, 5 Yellow, 6 Green).
Cape of Good Hope congestion High; week movement +15.3%.
CN feed: China shipbuilding orders nearly triple on Iran war windfall (Nikkei Asia).

logistics.summary: Logistics wire between war and prices is stable-ugly: Hormuz/Kerch Red, Bab el-Mandeb and Suez Yellow, Cape High congestion. Hormuz transit rebound (+68.2% WoW) and Bab +7.3% sit inside unchanged risk badges. Oil softens on flow and diplomacy hopes while the disruption scores do not. Partial coverage flags remain on several waterways.
cascadingImpacts: Tanker/war-risk → freight inflation → CPI with a lag
bullets: Hormuz +68.2%, Bab el-Mandeb +7.3%, Suez −8.9%, Kerch −100% week-over-week movement where published.
Cape of Good Hope congestion High on the same snapshot.

demographics.summary: No new UN/census global print in the pulse quotes. Displacement and fatality load stay in the crisis pages: Sudan 129 events / 314 fatalities; Red Sea tracker 960 fatalities; Horn of Africa 328 / 564 in the Sep HAPI month. JP typhoon is acute hazard, not a structural ageing print (last week’s centenarian item is not re-printed here).
cascadingImpacts: Conflict fatalities / displacement → labor and policy capacity on 2y–5y
bullets: Sudan crisis page: 129 events / 314 fatalities in the Sep HAPI month.
Horn of Africa 328 / 564 and Red Sea 659 / 960 on the same month pulse — humanitarian load, not a labor print.

public_policy.summary: Board this week is Duma continuity + US–Russia sanctions spillover + Trump–Xi prep + ICC sanctions readiness. RU feed: first State Duma election since the full-scale invasion; ruling party on track to keep majority. IN feed: India vows to protect energy security after new US tariffs over Russian oil; Modi in a bind on the Russia sanctions bill. Pulse headline: Trump administration readies sweeping ICC sanctions. CN: high-level talks ahead of Trump–Xi with LNG and AI safety on the table. Live FedWatch/CPI panels need authenticated WM access.
cascadingImpacts: Sanctions/tariffs + war premium → inflation expectations → G10 policy path; Trump–Xi LNG/AI talks → bilateral trade relief risk/reward
bullets: Russian State Duma election: same five parties set to return; ruling-party majority track (Meduza/AP).
India energy-security stance after US tariffs on Russian oil; Russia sanctions bill still binds Modi’s options.
Trump admin readies sweeping ICC sanctions (Al Jazeera); US–China high-level talks ahead of Trump–Xi (CN feed). Authenticated WM MCP/API not connected for FedWatch.

natural_resources.summary: Gold $4,399.3 (−0.58%; down from Sep 19’s $4,424.9); copper $6.732 (+0.61%; up from $6.6915). JP feed: China’s rare-earth trade limits still bite Japanese imports; Japan accelerates urban mining for critical metals. CN feed: Trump–Xi talks could mean ~$6B of US natural gas for China (Bloomberg). Public pulse did not publish stockpile/extraction series. Mining-tech: urban-mining acceleration is the concrete process item this week, not a new ore find.
cascadingImpacts: War bid softens → gold ease · rare-earth limits → Japan urban-mining / mineral-security capex · LNG deal talk → gas flow politics
bullets: Gold $4,399.3; copper $6.732 on the Sep 21 quote panel.
Japan rare-earth import squeeze and urban-mining push in the JP developments feed.
Trump–Xi LNG (~$6B US gas) item in CN feed; inventory/extraction series still need Pro/commodity sibling or MCP auth.

base: Hormuz stays Red; Brent holds a mid-to-high $90s neighborhood while diplomacy hopes and strong flows keep a soft bias under a 70 score.
Yemen High 70 and Iran High 70 keep Red Sea / Gulf insurance elevated; Ukraine stays Critical even after the ease to 82.
Russia sanctions spillover into India oil tariffs and Trump–Xi prep set the trade-policy tape.
ICC sanctions readiness and Duma continuity are political noise around the same war map.
risks: Hormuz closure or mine scare lasting more than a news cycle — diesel and Europe gas, not just Brent.
Houthi–Saudi spiral after the Riyadh attempt lifts Bab el-Mandeb toward Red.
Ukraine score re-accelerates after election-week strikes and forces a wider European security spend spike.

base: Oil war premium fades only with a secure Hormuz corridor or a real ceasefire — soft prints on diplomacy hopes are not that.
Cape rewiring stays a freight cost; Suez Yellow is relief, not normal.
Core inflation does not make a clean run at 2% while energy, freight, and tariffs bite.
US–China LNG/AI talks either deliver a limited bilateral package or stall into another tariff round.
risks: Second-round inflation if food freight and diesel stick via Kerch/Red Sea.
Europe winter gas if LNG routing and any Russia-gas political feelers stay messy.
Policy error — too slow on headline war inflation, too fast on labor.

base: 2026 Hormuz/Iran and Ukraine shocks remembered as mid-cycle supply breaks.
Capex gravitates to energy, grids, secured minerals, shipyards (China’s war windfall), and urban mining.
AI infra remains power-constrained; AI safety bilateral rules add compliance cost.
Chokepoint politics stay on the standing risk board.
risks: Real recession if tightening and oil run together.
Frozen Gulf conflict that institutionalizes high-$80s to ~$100 oil as normal.
Trade around the Cape for years, not weeks.

base: Chokepoint politics, mineral security, and dual-use shipyard capacity become standing features.
Demographics and public debt cap any 1970s policy replay.
Mining, refining, and urban reclaim capacity, not ore in the ground, set the resource constraint.
risks: A wider great-power war that takes the dashboard off monitor.
A clean peace plus productivity burst that collapses the war premium.
This brief would then look hawkish in hindsight.

cascadingImpacts: Iran/Hormuz + Yemen/Houthi + Ukraine → Hormuz/Kerch Red (Suez/Bab Yellow) → crude war premium (softening on diplomacy/flows) → headline CPI · inflation expectations → G10 policy path
Russia sanctions + India oil tariffs + Trump–Xi LNG/AI talks → trade friction or limited bilateral relief → freight and energy inflation with a lag
